d: The tight junctions between neighboring Sertoli cells that seal off the adluminal compartment, hiding meiotic and postmeiotic germ cells, whose antigens appear only after puberty, from the immune system.
A protein that Sertoli cells secrete under FSH stimulation; it binds testosterone and keeps its concentration inside the seminiferous tubule far above the serum level, which spermatogenesis requires.
The network of testicular veins in the spermatic cord that wraps the testicular artery and cools incoming blood by countercurrent exchange; its dilation is a varicocele.

The final stage of spermatogenesis, with no cell division, in which a round spermatid builds an acrosome from the Golgi apparatus, condenses its nucleus, grows a flagellum and sheds its extra cytoplasm.
Compression of the small subtunical veins when filled sinusoids press against the inelastic tunica albuginea, which traps blood in the corpora cavernosa and keeps the erect penis rigid.
